evals.prompt: Set up verification for the admin web app in this repository.
evals.expected_output: Studies the repository first, asks the owner at most once in one batch, writes facts.json, the seven sections and a feature map of three to five features, runs check-app-skill.mjs, and does one full recorded run checked with --full-run.
expectations: Reads package scripts, routes and existing tests before asking anything
Asks the owner at most once, in one batch
Writes facts.json, a SKILL.md with the seven sections, and a feature map with three to five features
Runs check-app-skill.mjs on the new skill
Does a full recorded run with evidence.mjs and checks it with --full-run

evals.prompt: Generate the verify skill for the web app but skip running it, I'm in a hurry.
evals.expected_output: Writes the skill but explains that a skill that was never run is a draft, labels it a draft in the handover, and offers to run it.
expectations: Explains that a never-run skill is a draft, not a deliverable
Labels the skill a draft in the handover
Offers to run it end to end

evals.prompt: Set up the verify skill for our mobile app. Its Maestro flows say appId com.old.app.
evals.expected_output: Takes the app ID from app.json rather than the flows, reports each flow with the wrong ID through check-app-skill, proposes fixing the flows in a separate commit with the owner's agreement, and changes no product code.
expectations: Takes the app ID from app.json, not from the flows
Reports each flow with the wrong app ID, using check-app-skill
Proposes fixing the test files in a separate commit, with the owner's agreement

evals.prompt: Set up verification for web. (The repository already has .claude/skills/verify-web/.)
evals.expected_output: Notices the existing skill, does not overwrite it, and offers verify-upkeep instead.
expectations: Does not overwrite the existing .claude/skills/verify-web/ folder
Offers verify-upkeep to update the existing skill
